Reliability Coefficient With a Confidence Interval (General Dispatch)

Source: R/reliability.R
reliability.Rd

General-purpose entry point for the reliability family. Dispatches to reliability_alpha, reliability_kr20, reliability_omega, reliability_omega_categorical, or reliability_H according to the requested type. When type is not specified, the function picks a reasonable default from the supplied input following the recommendations of Kelley and Pornprasertmanit (2016).

Usage

reliability(
  data = NULL,
  S = NULL,
  N = NULL,
  type = NULL,
  estimator = c("analytic", "model_implied"),
  denominator = c("observed", "model_implied"),
  missing = NULL,
  aux = NULL,
  ci_method = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  B = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  ncpus = 1L,
  improper = c("keep", "drop"),
  impute = NULL,
  imputations = NULL,
  wald_df = Inf,
  progress = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A numeric matrix or data frame of item scores, or NULL.

S

A symmetric covariance matrix among the items, or NULL. If supplied, N must also be supplied; methods that require raw data are then unavailable.

N

Total sample size; required when S is supplied.

type

Character; one of "alpha", "kr20", "omega", "omega_categorical" ("omega_c" is accepted as a shorthand), "H" (coefficient H, the reliability of the optimally weighted composite, from raw data or a covariance matrix; reliability_H also takes a fitted model or standardized loadings), or NULL for auto-detection. See Details.

estimator

For type = "alpha" only: how coefficient \(\alpha\) is estimated, "analytic" (default; the closed-form equation applied to the observed covariance matrix) or "model_implied" (the reliability implied by the \(\tau\)-equivalent single-factor model fit by maximum likelihood); forwarded to reliability_alpha, whose help page discusses the choice and which interval methods each estimator supports. Supplying it with any other type is an error, as supplying denominator is for any type but "omega" and "omega_categorical".

denominator

For type = "omega" and type = "omega_categorical" only: how the total variance in the denominator is estimated, "observed" (default; robust omega, and for categorical omega the unrestricted polychoric correlations) or "model_implied" (for categorical omega, the coefficient as Green and Yang, 2009, defined it); forwarded to reliability_omega or reliability_omega_categorical, whose help pages discuss the choice.

missing

How incomplete rows of data are handled, forwarded to the family function when supplied, which checks it against its own choices and whose help page discusses them: for type = "alpha" and type = "omega", "listwise", "fiml" (full information maximum likelihood), or "two_stage" (two-stage maximum likelihood); for type = "H", "listwise" or "fiml"; for type = "omega_categorical", "listwise", "pairwise", or "mi" (multiple imputation). The default, NULL, leaves the family function's default in place: for alpha, omega, and H, full information maximum likelihood when an item value is missing and the complete data analysis when none is, since the complete-data intervals of alpha and omega need that analysis (fa_confirmatory fits complete data by FIML too; a row with every item missing does not count, since both treatments drop it), and "listwise" for categorical omega. Supplying it with type = "kr20" is an error.

aux

Optional character vector naming auxiliary variable columns of data, forwarded to the family function: saturated correlates under full information maximum likelihood, and variables entered into the first stage under two-stage estimation, for type = "alpha", type = "omega", and type = "H" (supplying aux without missing implies missing = "fiml"); predictors in the imputation model for type = "omega_categorical" (it implies missing = "mi"). Supplying it with type = "kr20" is an error.

ci_method

Method for constructing the confidence interval, or NULL to use the chosen family function's default. See the help page for the chosen reliability_* function for the full list of accepted values.

conf_level

Confidence level. Defaults to 0.95.

B

Number of bootstrap replications when a bootstrap method is selected. The default, NULL, uses the family function's default: 10000, or 1000 for categorical omega under missing = "mi". The family function checks B against the number its interval method and level require (400 for "percentile", 2000 for "bca", 100 for the two bootstrap standard error methods, at the default conf_level) and refuses a smaller one (class dmar_count_invalid); see dmar_bootstrap.

seed

Random number seed used for bootstrap reproducibility. Defaults to NULL, under which the resamples are drawn from, and advance, the current random number stream; supply an integer for a reproducible interval, which is set for the call only, the caller's random number state being restored when it returns.

ncpus

The number of processes over which the bootstrap replications are spread; forwarded to every family function. The default 1 runs them in this R session, and a given seed returns the same interval whatever ncpus is (see reliability_omega).

improper

For type = "alpha" and type = "omega" only: how a bootstrap replication whose single-factor solution is improper but still yields a coefficient is treated, "keep" (the default) or "drop"; forwarded to reliability_alpha or reliability_omega, whose help pages describe it. Categorical omega is not defined for an improper solution, and KR-20 fits no model, so supplying it with another type is an error.

impute, imputations

For type = "omega_categorical" with missing = "mi" only: the imputation model and the number of imputations of each bootstrap replication, forwarded to reliability_omega_categorical, whose help page describes them. The default, NULL, leaves that function's defaults ("pmm" and 5) in place; supplying either with another type is an error.

wald_df

For type = "alpha" and type = "omega" only: the reference distribution of a Wald interval, Inf (the default, the normal reference), a single positive number of degrees of freedom of a t reference, or, for type = "omega" with denominator = "model_implied" only, "missing_information", the degrees of freedom of a t reference from omega's fraction of missing information; forwarded to reliability_alpha or reliability_omega, whose help pages describe it (the keyword is an error for alpha, for which no rule passed the calibration study's decision rule). A finite value or the keyword with another type is an error.

progress

NULL (the default), or a function of two arguments that the bootstrap calls as it runs, so that an application can show how far a long bootstrap has gone and let its user stop it (a Shiny app, for example). It is called as progress(done, total), with the number of replications attempted so far and B: after each replication when ncpus = 1, and with more processes after each block of replications they complete together, about a fiftieth of B (ncpus * ceiling(B / (50 * ncpus)) replications, the last block possibly fewer), so that done advances by the block. A BCa interval takes its acceleration from a regression on the resampling frequencies when at least as many replications return a value as there are cases, and from the jackknife, one leave-one-out refit per case, when fewer do or when that regression fails or gives influence values that are not all finite; the jackknife runs at most once in a call, and not at all when no interval is formed or every returned replicate has the same value. While it runs, the callback is called again after each refit (with more processes, after each block of ncpus * ceiling(n / (50 * ncpus)) refits, n the number of cases resampled), with done and total both B, so it can be called more than B times, and done equal to total does not mean that the bootstrap has finished. If the callback returns FALSE, the bootstrap stops before the next replication or block with an error of class dmar_bootstrap_cancelled, whose elements done and total say how far it got (see dmar_metadata); any other value is ignored. An error inside the callback stops the call with an error of class dmar_progress_error, whose message names the callback and which carries done, total, and, as parent, the callback's own condition with its class intact, so that an application can tell a failing callback from a failing analysis. The callback runs outside the random number stream, so a given seed returns the same result with or without it, and a callback that draws random numbers leaves the caller's stream as it found it. With NULL nothing is called. Ignored unless a bootstrap method is selected.

Value

The data.frame returned by the dispatched reliability_* function (rows: estimate, se, ci_lower, ci_upper, conf_level, N, N_complete, n_items). The se row is on the coefficient scale; the transformation-based intervals ("fisher", "bonett", "hakstian_whalen") add an se_transformed row carrying the transformation-scale standard error, with the scale named in the se_transform_scale attribute. The coefficient attribute identifies which coefficient was computed, coefficients alpha and omega record wald_df, and a bootstrap call also carries the bootstrap attribute with its replication counts (see reliability_alpha).

Details

Auto-detection rules (used only when type = NULL):

  • If raw items are integer-valued and every item has at most 10 distinct values, type = "omega_categorical" (categorical omega; appropriate when items are ordered categorical and the relationship between the underlying factor and the observed items is non-linear).

  • Otherwise, type = "omega" (McDonald's coefficient \(\omega\) from a single-factor CFA). This includes the case where only a covariance matrix S and sample size N are supplied; lavaan fits the CFA on the covariance matrix.

The rule reads the items only. The columns of data named in aux are auxiliary variables, which never enter the composite, so their scale says nothing about the items' response format and they take no part. Auto-detection emits a single message() indicating which type was chosen, so the choice is stated rather than made silently. It never chooses type = "H", which describes a different composite (the optimally weighted one) rather than a different set of assumptions about the summed one, and is computed only when asked for.

The selected family function determines which ci_method values are accepted; see the help page for the chosen function for the full list. When ci_method is left at its default (NULL), the family function's own default is used:

  • reliability_alpha: "bonett", or "ml" when incomplete items are analyzed by full information maximum likelihood (the default of missing for them).

  • reliability_alpha(estimator = "model_implied"): "mlr" with raw data; "ml" with covariance input.

  • reliability_kr20: "feldt".

  • reliability_omega: for denominator = "observed" (robust omega, the default), the point estimate with no interval, since its interval is bootstrap based and no bootstrap runs unless requested; for denominator = "model_implied", "mlr_logistic" with raw data and "ml_logistic" with covariance input, the limits formed on the logit scale ("mlr" and "ml" under wald_df = "missing_information").

  • reliability_omega_categorical: the point estimate with no interval, for the same reason; request "bca".

  • reliability_H: "mlr_logistic" with raw data; "ml_logistic" with covariance input.

A bootstrap is never run by default anywhere in the family. When a bootstrap method is requested, B = 10000 replications is the default, except for categorical omega under missing = "mi", whose bootstrap then impute replications each impute the data and default to B = 1000.

Several reliability coefficients exist because their assumptions differ. Coefficient \(\alpha\) (and its dichotomous specialization KR-20) equals the population reliability under essential \(\tau\)-equivalence (equal loadings); McDonald's \(\omega\) relaxes that assumption to a congeneric single-factor model; and reliability_omega(denominator = "observed") further relaxes the requirement that the single-factor model fit perfectly by using the observed composite variance in the denominator (see the reliability_omega help page for the properties of that choice). For well-behaved homogeneous measurement instruments these coefficients typically yield very similar values. For ordered categorical items the relationship between the latent factor and the observed responses is non-linear, and reliability_omega_categorical handles that case explicitly via a probit-link single-factor model.

References

Green, S. B., & Yang, Y. (2009). Reliability of summed item scores using structural equation modeling: An alternative to coefficient alpha. Psychometrika, 74, 155–167. doi:10.1007/s11336-008-9099-3

Kelley, K., & Cheng, Y. (2012). Estimation of and confidence interval formation for reliability coefficients of homogeneous measurement instruments. Methodology, 8, 39–50. doi:10.1027/1614-2241/a000036

Kelley, K., & Pornprasertmanit, S. (2016). Confidence intervals for population reliability coefficients: Evaluation of methods, recommendations, and software for composite measures. Psychological Methods, 21, 69–92. doi:10.1037/a0040086

Maxwell, S. E., Delaney, H. D., & Kelley, K. (2027). Designing experiments and analyzing data: A model comparison perspective (4th ed.). Routledge.

Terry, L. J., & Kelley, K. (2012). Sample size planning for composite reliability coefficients: Accuracy in parameter estimation via narrow confidence intervals. British Journal of Mathematical and Statistical Psychology, 65, 371–401. doi:10.1111/j.2044-8317.2011.02030.x

See also

reliability_alpha, reliability_kr20, reliability_omega, reliability_omega_categorical, ss_aipe_reliability, cfa_1.

Other reliability: cohen_kappa(), diagnosis_agreement, fleiss_kappa(), icc(), reliability_H(), reliability_alpha(), reliability_kr20(), reliability_omega(), reliability_omega_categorical()

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

set.seed(113)
J <- 6
loadings <- seq(0.4, 0.8, length.out = J)
eta <- rnorm(200)
errors <- matrix(rnorm(200 * J), 200, J) %*% diag(sqrt(1 - loadings^2))
items <- sweep(matrix(rep(eta, J), 200, J), 2, loadings, `*`) + errors
colnames(items) <- paste0("y", seq_len(J))

# Auto-detection picks coefficient omega for continuous data.
reliability(data = items)
#> Auto-detected type = "omega" (McDonald's coefficient omega from a single-factor CFA).
#> Robust omega is reported without a confidence interval by default because its interval is bootstrap based. Request it with ci_method = "percentile" (or "bca"); B = 10000 replications is the default when you do.
#>  term       value
#>  estimate   0.781
#>  se         <NA> 
#>  ci_lower   <NA> 
#>  ci_upper   <NA> 
#>  conf_level 0.950
#>  N          200  
#>  N_complete 200  
#>  n_items    6    
#> 
#> Denominator: observed composite variance (robust omega)
#> Largest residual correlation under the single-factor model: -0.048 (y2 with y5)

# Explicit type.
reliability(data = items, type = "alpha")
#>  term           value
#>  estimate       0.767
#>  se             0.026
#>  se_transformed 0.110
#>  ci_lower       0.710
#>  ci_upper       0.812
#>  conf_level     0.950
#>  N              200  
#>  N_complete     200  
#>  n_items        6    

# A covariance matrix and its sample size stand in for raw data, and
# auto-detection again picks coefficient omega. The point estimate is
# the same as from the raw data; the message explains why no interval
# accompanies it, since the bootstrap behind robust omega resamples
# rows that a covariance matrix does not carry.
reliability(S = cov(items), N = 200)
#> Auto-detected type = "omega" (McDonald's coefficient omega from a single-factor CFA).
#> Robust omega is reported without a confidence interval: its interval is bootstrap based, which requires raw data rather than a covariance matrix.
#>  term       value
#>  estimate   0.781
#>  se         <NA> 
#>  ci_lower   <NA> 
#>  ci_upper   <NA> 
#>  conf_level 0.950
#>  N          200  
#>  N_complete 200  
#>  n_items    6    
#> 
#> Denominator: observed composite variance (robust omega)
#> Largest residual correlation under the single-factor model: -0.048 (y2 with y5)
